sources.note: Nothing on stress. States the total documentation: 'Two short wordlists were compiled by Conrad & Dye (1975) and Laycock (1972), and the latter included a sentence or two on grammar in a later work (1975b:854). Further, an unpublished 200-word list was collected by Arjen Lock in 1992.' Table 1: Pyu = 'Short wordlist', highly endangered.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. 2010. Pyu Swadesh List (pby), archive.org rosettaproject_pby_swadesh-1 (no source given).
sources.note: No statement. Merged list from unstated sources; one strand carries acute accents (máru 'bird', kəlísí 'black', kamí 'blood', bəlí 'bone', napú 'child', lisí 'hair', kabyí 'hand', talí 'man'), which neither Voorhoeve's nor Conrad & Dye's printed lists show; origin unverified (possibly Laycock 1972 original), so not usable as evidence.

sources.citation: Steer, Martin. 2005. Languages of the Upper Sepik and Central New Guinea. Report prepared for the Upper Sepik-Central New Guinea Project, South Australian Museum, September 2005; edits and Appendix 9.2 by B. Craig 2011. 60 pp. (Pyu named at sec. 6.1 Abau, p. ~24, and sec. 8.2 Yuri/Karkar, p. ~41.)
sources.note: no phonology content for Pyu: the language is named only as a neighbour ('The neighbouring languages are Pyu (south and west, mainly in [West] Papua); Biksi (west)..' sec. 6.1; 'Neighbouring languages are Emumu (west), the Senagi family (north and east), Abau (south), Pyu (south-west) (Information from LAP)' sec. 8.2). No Pyu wordlist, no Pyu bibliography entry; the phonology remarks in the report (sec. 7.4, and the Price 1981 'Determining stress in Karkar', Steinkraus 'Tifal tone' references) concern other languages.

sources.citation: Baron, Wietze. 1983. Kwomtari Survey. Unpublished ms., Summer Institute of Linguistics, Ukarumpa, Papua New Guinea. 44 pp. (PDF typeset 2008; Pyu: note 9, pp. 37-38).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No prose statement about Pyu stress or tone. Note 9 (p. 37): '9) Laycock ('75a) also includes the Pyu language in this phylum. As we only have the short wordlist on this language published in Laycock ('72), it is left out of this discussion. Items in the list corresponding with the ones employed for this survey are given below..'. The 40-item Pyu list on p. 38 is headed 'Note: underscore marks stress!' and, checked on the 300-dpi page scan, carries underlining on five forms only: tal_i_ 'man', na_pu_ 'child', təp_li_ 'nose', bə_rna_ 'eye', kab_yi_ 'hand' (stress-marked syllable final in all f…

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18, 1-35. Pacific Linguistics A-40 (Pyu: sec. 3.5 p. 13; fn. 24 p. 20; Table 2 wordlist pp. 25-29).
sources.note: No stress statement for Pyu. The one phonology note (Figure C, p. 10) concerns the Arai family only ('Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga'). The Pyu column of the ~110-item wordlist (pp. 25-29, checked on page scan) carries no stress marks; sec. 3.5 says only that Pyu is spoken at Biake No. 2 and Buriap and is 0-3% cognate with everything else.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Pyu' (glottocode pyuu1245, ISO pby): lexicon from Conrad & Dye (1975) and Voorhoeve (1975). Accessed 2026-09-20.
sources.note: wordlist-only: phonetic forms (e.g. maľuľiʔ 'bird', kʌbi duhʌnɛʔ 'arm', tɛᵽiɛʔ 'one') retyped from the two 1975 printed lists; no stress or tone marks and no prose.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology. Only typological remarks: 'Fas, Kwomtari and Pyu appear to have no concordance in verbs with either subject or object'; 'A first wordlist of Pyu was given by Laycock (1972), and a more extensive list (about 110 items) is given by Conrad and Dye (1975).'
